title: Does Physical Restraint Use Prevent Falls in Nursing Homes?
text: Physical restraint use nursing homes common controversial practice. One frequently cited justifications fall prevention. analysis examines whether facility-level restraint prevalence associated lower fall rates, using longitudinal data 2016 2025 across nursing homes province Trento, Italy.

title: Does Physical Restraint Use Prevent Falls in Nursing Homes?
text: Data come Indicare Salute Lab quality monitoring system. observation represents facility × care-sector × month combination, pairing restraint indicator (2.1, point prevalence index day) three nested fall indicators: total falls (1.1), falls outcome (1.3), falls major outcome fractures (1.5). nesting (1.5⊆1.3⊆1.11.5 \subseteq 1.3 \subseteq 1.1) allows outcome cells modeled single multinomial vector residents.

Conditional observed restraint count XX facility–sector pair kk: X∼Binomial(nx,pk),Y∣X∼Binomial(ny,p‾k),p‾k=Xnxqk+(1−Xnx)rk X \sim \text{Binomial}(n_x, p_k), \qquad Y \mid X \sim \text{Binomial}\!\left(n_y,\; \bar p_k\right), \quad \bar p_k = \frac{X}{n_x}\, q_k + \left(1 - \frac{X}{n_x}\right) r_k qkq_k rkr_k fall probabilities restrained non-restrained residents. Fall outcomes factorized exactly Binomial(fall) × Multinomial(outcome | fall), outcome cells (outcome / minor / major). Restraint prevalence follows per-pair quadratic time trend logit scale (orthogonalized standardized), logit(pk)=βk+αkt+γkt2\text{logit}(p_k) = \beta_k + \alpha_k t + \gamma_k t^2; fall rates partially pooled across pairs via Beta hyperpriors, outcome shares via non-centered logistic-normal hierarchy.

title: Does Physical Restraint Use Prevent Falls in Nursing Homes?
text: association restraint falls strongly heterogeneous across facility–sector pairs. 47 pairs, 15 show credible benefit (restrained residents fall less), 8 show credible harm, rest uncertain — effect changes sign across facilities. new, unobserved facility–sector pair, posterior predictive probability benefit 61%. major-outcome falls (clinically important ones), average effect compatible zero predictive evidence benefit weak (P ≈ 0.60). falls minor outcomes, pairs show credible harm (10) credible benefit (6).

title: Does Physical Restraint Use Prevent Falls in Nursing Homes?
text: effect physical restraint falls real generalizable: sign magnitude vary unpredictably across facilities. meaningful evidence restraint reduces falls matter — major outcomes. Effectiveness fall-prevention strategy evaluated case case, based characteristics facility, confirmed individual-level data.

title: Physical Restraint Use and Falls in Nursing Homes
text: Data come Indicare Salute Lab, quality monitoring system managed UPIPA (Unione Provinciale Istituzioni Per l’Assistenza). Observations facility × care-sector × month combinations, pairing restraint indicator (2.1, point prevalence) three nested fall indicators: total falls (1.1), falls outcome (1.3), falls major outcome fractures (1.5). main research question whether physical restraint use associated reduction falls — whether association clinically meaningful.

title: Physical Restraint Use and Falls in Nursing Homes
text: restraint–fall association strongly heterogeneous across facility–sector pairs generalizable: 47 facility–sector pairs, ~15 show credible benefit, ~8 credible harm, ~24 uncertain — effect changes sign across facilities. new, unobserved facility, posterior predictive probability benefit ~61%. meaningful evidence restraint reduces major-outcome falls (clinically important ones): average effect compatible zero. minor-outcome falls, pairs show credible harm (10) credible benefit (6). Effectiveness restraint fall-prevention strategy evaluated case case, based characteristics facility, confirmed individual-level data.

title: Physical Restraint Use and Falls in Nursing Homes
text: Bayesian hierarchical models estimated Stan (cmdstanr). final model uses collapsed likelihood — falls conditional observed restraint count, Y∣X∼Bin(ny,p‾)Y \mid X \sim \text{Bin}(n_y, \bar p) p‾=(X/nx)q+(1−X/nx)r\bar p = (X/n_x)\,q + (1 - X/n_x)\,r — nested fall outcomes factorized exactly Binomial(fall) × Multinomial(outcome | fall). Restraint prevalence follows per-pair quadratic time trend (orthogonalized, standardized); fall rates partially pooled across facility–sector pairs via Beta hyperpriors, outcome shares via non-centered logistic-normal hierarchy. Model development proceeded 12 iterations Bayes factors (bridge sampling) posterior predictive checks; full workflow documented data-raw/model-development.qmd.

One : 1.1 Residenti caduti nel periodo di riferimento (residents fell reference period) 1.3 Cadute con esito (falls injury) 1.5 Cadute con esito maggiore (falls major injury) 2.1 Persone soggette contenzione fisica (residents subject physical restraint) id_settore Care unit identifier within facility n Numerator. Meaning depends indicatore: 1.1 Number residents least one registered fall reference period 1.3 Number falls injury (minor + major) reference period 1.5 Number falls major injury reference period 2.1 Number residents active physical restraint prescription index day d Denominator.
